We present a methodology for selecting a network model from a set of network models, given a set of tasks and task neighborhoods, for the purpose of predicting task performance.

(1) network model selection for task-focused network inference improves predictive performance by up to an order of magnitude, (2) model selection criteria can be evaluated on their ability to predict the best model for a given task, and (3) the best network model for one task may not generalize well to another task.
